lead.basis: The order's only operative content amends, modifies or restates part of another order or regulation, or substitutes a date in it; under P2 (D-20261021-strike-and-insert) it merges into the parent on issue: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it. A later order that amends or supersedes the amended text acts on the parent, so held amendment edges dated after the order's date do not keep the member alive.

sources.citation: The member order's own held text

gaps: Disclosure: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it.
If the owner treats an amending order as living as long as the amended text lives, these leads become open pending the parent (P2 adoption choice).

Several members state an effective date different from their signing date (EO 552 from July 1, 1907; EO 3864 from September 1, 1923; EO 4473 from July 1, 1926; EO 3024B as of the parent's date); P2 dates the merger by the amending order's own date, and the stated date governs when the amended text operated within the parent.

Held amendment edges dated after the order act on the parent, not on the member: EO 574 restates EO 552's amendment of the Hot Springs rules; EO 6561 defers again the abolition date that EO 6512 set in EO 6433-A; EO 6683 and EO 6788 amend EO 6474 as amended by EO 6576; EO 7164 recites Regulations No. 1 and No. 2 'as amended' by EO 7117, 7119 and 7125. The engine flags these six members; the flags do not change the leads.
